skill.name: brainstorming
skill.description: Guides collaborative brainstorming before software changes by clarifying intent, exploring approaches, and turning decisions into a design document.
skill.summary: Plan software changes through questions, options, tradeoffs, and validated design notes.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. The flagged backticks are a markdown code span for a documentation path, not shell execution. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed skill text.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 38 uses backticks only to format the path docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md in markdown. It does not execute Ruby, shell commands, or user-controlled input.

content.value_statement: Software ideas can move to implementation before goals and tradeoffs are clear. This skill guides structured questions, approach comparison, and validated design notes.
actual_capabilities: Prompts the assistant to inspect project context before proposing changes.
Guides one question at a time to clarify goals, constraints, and success criteria.
Compares two or three possible approaches with tradeoffs and a recommendation.
Structures design sections covering architecture, components, data flow, errors, and tests.
Directs the assistant to save the validated design as a planning document.
limitations: It does not implement code changes by itself.
It depends on user answers to refine the design.
It does not validate technical feasibility outside the available project context.
It may require separate planning skills before implementation continues.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Feature
use_cases.description: Clarify user goals, constraints, and design choices before development begins.

use_cases.title: Compare Product Approaches
use_cases.description: Explore several implementation paths and select one with clear tradeoffs.

use_cases.title: Create Design Records
use_cases.description: Turn a validated discussion into a concise design document for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Start Feature Brainstorming
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to help plan a new feature. First inspect the project context, then ask me one question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a rough idea into clear requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to refine this idea into goals, constraints, success criteria, and open questions before any implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Design Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to propose two or three approaches, explain tradeoffs, and recommend one option with reasoning.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Implementation Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a validated design for a complex change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to create a design in sections covering architecture, components, data flow, error handling, and testing.

output_examples.input: I want to add saved filters to a dashboard.
output: The assistant first checks the project context.
It asks one focused question about who uses saved filters.
It compares local, server, and shared filter designs.
It drafts a design section for validation.

output_examples.input: We need a better onboarding flow, but the scope is unclear.
output: The assistant asks for the primary onboarding goal.
It identifies constraints such as account setup, tracking, and support load.
It recommends a practical first version.
It records the agreed design in a planning document.

best_practices: Answer each question with concrete goals, constraints, and examples.
Ask for tradeoffs when several approaches seem reasonable.
Validate each design section before moving to implementation planning.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation before the design has clear success criteria.
Answering several unrelated questions in one response.
Using the skill for final code review instead of early design exploration.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps turn a software idea into a clearer design before implementation starts.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on discovery, design options, tradeoffs, and planning notes.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the assistant to inspect project context before asking design questions.

faq.question: How does it handle complex ideas?
faq.answer: It breaks the discussion into small questions and validates design sections incrementally.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before building features, changing behavior, or documenting a new technical approach.
